questions.problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=(t+2)\,i+(\sqrt{2}t-2)\,j-t\,k,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=2t$, find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, since $s=2t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{2}.$

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{s}{2}+2)i+(\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{s}{2}-2)j-\frac{s}{2}\,k \\  & =(\frac{s+4}{2})i+(\frac{\sqrt{2}s-4}{2})j-\frac{s}{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s+4}{2})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}s-4}{2})j-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s}{2})k \\  & =\frac{1}{2}i+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,j-\frac{1}{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{4})\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{4})\,j,$  $\,t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{4}))i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{4}))j \\  & =-4{t}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{4})\,i+4{t}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{4})\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{[-4{t}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{4})]}^{2}+{[4{t}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{4})]}^{2}} \\  & =4|t{|}^{3}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{4})+{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{4})} \\  & =4{t}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}4{u}^{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={u}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & ={t}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

  

Now, since $s={t}^{4}$, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{4} & =s \\ t & =\sqrt[4]{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt[4]{s}) \\  & =cos\,((\sqrt[4]{s})^{4})\,i+sin\,((\sqrt[4]{s})^{4})\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(s)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(s)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨t\sqrt{5},\,-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=3t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, since $s=3t,$ we have that $t=\frac{s}{3}.$

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{3}) \\  & =⟨\frac{s\sqrt{5}}{3},\,-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3}),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parameterized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s\sqrt{5}}{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3},\,\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}),\,\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\sqrt{5},\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2,\,1-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t+9{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{9({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}3\,\text{d}u \\  & =3u\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =3t\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s=3t,$ we have that $t=\frac{s}{3}.$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{3}) \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})-2,\,1-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨\frac{4}{3}(1+t)^{3/2},\,t,\,\frac{4}{3}(1-t)^{3/2}⟩,$ $-1\le t\le 1,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=3t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, since $s=3t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{3}.$

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{3}) \\  & =⟨\frac{4}{3}{(1+\frac{s}{3})}^{3/2},\,\frac{s}{3},\,\frac{4}{3}{(1-\frac{s}{3})}^{3/2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parameterized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{3}{(1+\frac{s}{3})}^{3/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s}{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{3}{(1+\frac{s}{3})}^{3/2})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{1+\frac{s}{3}},\,\frac{1}{3},\,-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{1-\frac{s}{3}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}}⟨\sqrt{3+s},\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\sqrt{3-s}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
